title: Quantile-focused experiment scheduling and evaluation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Playbook for scheduling and evaluating rollout experiments with a focus on quantile-based SLAs and tail-risk mitigation. This doc defines the end-to-end cadence for preflight simulation, staged traffic shifts, realtime quantile monitoring, and decision triggers (promote/hold/rollback). It standardizes artifacts (synthetic smoke scripts, quantile dashboards, canary cohorts) so PMs and Eng can run deterministic rollouts across Dedicated and Hosted deployments.
background: Recent incidents highlighted that mean/p50-based gating missed regressions in p95/p99 token latency and long-tail correctness. We need a reproducible experiment flow that prioritizes quantiles, ties quality regressions to prompt-level evals, and enforces explicit risk budgets for each rollout stage.
goals: Ensure canaries detect regressions at p95 and p99 before wider traffic shifts
Reduce time-to-decision with preflight simulations that approximate production tail behavior
Provide a clear promote/hold/rollback rubric tied to customer-impact buckets and risk budgets
Make playbook usable across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments
milestones: 2026-01-20: Finalize quantile metric definitions (p50/p90/p95/p99) and mapping to SLO bands
2026-01-28: Implement synthetic preflight harness with configurable load/seq-length distributions
2026-02-05: Launch dashboard templates for quantile-focused monitoring (per-route + global)
2026-02-15: Run three shadow experiments to validate simulation fidelity against production traces
2026-02-22: Approve rollout rubric and publish playbook to Confluence
2026-03-01: Pilot the playbook on a low-risk feature and capture learnings
evaluation_metrics: p50 latency delta (baseline vs candidate, ms)
semantic-regression rate on canonical prompt suite (% of prompts with unacceptable deviation)
cost per 1k tokens (USD), delta vs baseline
user-visible throughput (requests/minute) under SLO traffic profile
instrumentation_tasks: Add quantile time-series to per-route dashboard (p50/p90/p95/p99) with 1-minute resolution
Tag canary traffic in tracing so distribution can be compared to baseline cohorts
Add synthetic preflight scripts for three canonical workloads: short-chat, long-doc, embeddings-bulk
Export prompt-level golden set results to Eval service for semantic regression checks
Create alert rules for quantile breaches and rate-of-change anomalies
Populate canary run metadata (build, model commit, config flags) into experiment index
rollback_triggers: p99 latency increase > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets
p95 latency increase > 50% sustained for 10 minutes
Error rate increase > 0.5 percentage points absolute and customer-impact is high
Semantic-regression rate on canonical prompts > 1% and failing clusters are user-facing intents
Automated circuit-breaker if combined risk budget consumption > 80% in stage
escalation_paths: Stage 1: Canary owner inspects dashboards and synthetic runs (owner: ENG oncall)
Stage 2: If rollback threshold met, page SRE and PM (severity: P1)
Stage 3: If semantic regressions detected, involve Applied ML and Research for triage
Stage 4: Executive notification if > 5% production traffic impacted or SLA breach projected
decision_rubric: Green: All quantiles within SLO bands and semantic-regression delta < 0.1% => Promote to next stage
Amber: Minor p95 drift (<20%) but semantic tests pass => Hold and run extended observation + simulation
Red: Any p99 breach beyond threshold or semantic-regression > 1% => Rollback immediately
Cost override: If cost delta > 30% and no user-visible improvement, hold and consult PM for business trade-off
communication_plan: Pre-launch: Publish plan and expected risk budget to Slack #prod-experiments and Confluence
During canary: Post hourly updates with quantile snapshots and synthetic-run summaries
On decision: Document reason for promote/hold/rollback in experiment index and link PRs
Postmortem: If rollback or SLA miss, produce short incident learnings and update playbook
notes: Trade-offs: tighter p99 gates reduce risk but increase false positives and rollout friction
Mitigation: use simulation-derived muting rules for low-risk noise patterns before deciding
We purposefully separate semantic-eval failures from latency regressions; both must be considered in rubric
This playbook is intentionally conservative for first two quarters and will relax thresholds after 3 validated pilots
